equals.title: AI Made Execution Cheap. High-Stakes Decisions Are Still Expensive.
equals.stage: M4 · Machine Learning, Generative & Agentic AI
equals.summary: I presented the AI-Native Product OS, then applied its Stack and Loop to a hypothetical $4.2 billion cross-border payment in a simulated bank workflow. The example shows why an ambiguous sanctions match needs an evaluation case and a system-enforced escalation rule, regardless of the model’s confidence.

takeaways: The Stack helps locate a decision or failure across model, context, orchestration, governance and human responsibility.
The Loop makes scope, acceptance criteria and observations part of development, rather than treating a convincing output as enough.
A model’s confidence does not authorise a payment. Approval requirements and escalation rules belong in the surrounding system.

workedExample.title: Find the bottleneck before choosing the automation
workedExample.body: A hypothetical Dubai treasury team needs to prepare a $4.2 billion cross-border payment. The team first asks whether documents, conflicting information, liquidity or approvals are causing the delay.

workedExample.title: Scope the assistant to an evidence-backed recommendation
workedExample.body: The proposed assistant reads the supplied evidence and drafts a recommendation brief, with a simulated handoff into the workflow. It does not gain independent authority to move funds.
workedExample.artifact: A bounded task and agreed acceptance criteria.

workedExample.title: Define who can authorise and what must stop the workflow
workedExample.body: The scenario puts transaction limits, mandatory checks and required approvals outside the model. The workflow preserves transaction references for safe retries and records evidence, actions and approvals.

workedExample.title: Expose the ambiguous sanctions match
workedExample.body: In the teaching scenario, the model confidently treats a partial counterparty-name match as a different organisation. The proposed workflow lacks an escalation rule for that ambiguity, so confidence is allowed to stand in for a control.
workedExample.artifact: A specific failure case, rather than a vague concern about AI.

workedExample.title: Turn the failure into an evaluation case
workedExample.body: The talk proposes a set of known ambiguous sanctions cases whose expected behaviour is escalation. This defines a testable requirement; it is not a published dataset or a measured pass rate.
workedExample.artifact: Expected behaviour: escalate the ambiguous case.

workedExample.title: Enforce escalation independently of confidence
workedExample.body: The proposed rule routes a partial match above a defined similarity threshold to a human compliance officer. The model may still read, synthesise and draft; it cannot override the escalation rule.
workedExample.artifact: An escalation rule enforced outside the model.

workedExample.title: Rerun the scenario against the revised control
workedExample.body: The script describes replaying the same hypothetical case with escalation before approval. In a real product, the team would need recorded test results, wider failure coverage and release criteria before relying on that control.
workedExample.artifact: An illustrative rerun, with real validation still required.
